newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: HERMIS BANK'S 1Q NET PROFIT RISES.
newsitem.headline: HERMIS BANK'S 1Q NET PROFIT RISES.

text.p: Lithuania's second largest private commercial bank, Hermis Bank, said on Tuesday that its unaudited 1Q net profit for 1997 was 9.3 million litas versus 4.4 million litas for the same period last year.
The chairwoman of the bank's board, Dr. Nadiezhda Novickiene, also told Reuters that the bank's deposits rose to 451 million litas from 413.9 million litas in the first three months of the year.
She added that its loan portfolio grew by 23 percent to 285 million litas during the first quarter of 1997.
"Our bank has been operating more professionally this year than last year and we are more effective in earning income and controlling expenses," she said.
"I am sure that we will reach our strategic aim to control around 20 percent of the country's banking market before 2001," she said.
She did not say what the bank's current market share is.
The bank's net profit last year soared to over 27 million litas after a loss of over nine million litas in 1995.
